title.narrative: Provision of integrated life-saving WASH assistance to the most vulnerable communities in under-served and hard-to-reach rural areas in Beletweyne, Hiran

description.narrative: ltpgtSomalia continues to grapple with a severe water crisis due to consecutive failed rainy seasons, with the Deyr 2024 rains were erratic and poorly distributed, particularly affecting regions like Hirshabelle, which received significantly below-normal precipitation. This has led to a decline in groundwater levels, severely impacting rural communities that depend on shallow wells and seasonal water sources. The anticipated below-average rainfall and rising temperatures are expected to worsen drought conditions, further straining limited water resources, reducing access to safe water and sanitation services, and increasing the risk of disease outbreaks. In response, Save the Children (SC) proposes a life-saving WASH intervention targeting the most vulnerable populations, including men, women, boys, and girls in underserved, hard-to-reach rural areas of Beletweyne district to mitigate the effects of dry conditions and displacement. The project aims to improve access to safe drinking water and sanitation, promote safe hygiene practices, and improve waste management to reduce public health risks and meet urgent needs. This will be achieved through the rehabilitation of 2 existing water sources, implementation of 1 pipeline extension and improvement of water systems serving households, schools, and health/nutrition facilities, and the provision of 3 sets of spare parts and accessories to ensure the functionality and sustainability of water systems and scaling up water quality monitoring and treatment. Additionally, WASH support will be provided to 5 health facilities to strengthen IPC. The project will also construct 60 emergency latrines that are accessible to people living with disabilities (PLWD) and equipped with handwashing facilities, rehabilitate 40 existing latrines in IDP settlements, distribute 94 sanitation tools, and organize 25 regular community clean-up campaigns. Community hygiene promotion campaigns will be conducted by 28 trained hygiene promoters, and 1500 hygiene kits sourced from the regional hub will be distributed to promote improved hygiene practices, household water treatment, and safe water storage. These interventions align with the 2025 WASH Cluster allocation strategy and joint assessment findings in Hiran. Beneficiaries will be identified through consultations with community leaders, local authorities, ABC focal points, and cluster coordinators, ensuring coordination and integration with sectors such as FSL, Health, Nutrition, and Protection. Special attention will be given to gender considerations by ensuring that women and g]irls actively participate in assessments, planning, and monitoring, promoting over 50% female participation among hygiene promoters, and providing gender-segregated latrines located near households to reduce the risk of GBV. The project will also empower women and persons with disabilities, adhering to protection principles to ensure safe and equitable access to services while minimizing future risks. Over a 12-month period, the project will benefit 14,256 vulnerable individuals, including 3,421 men, 3,565 women, 3,563 boys, and 3,707 girls by enhancing access to essential WASH services and improving health and dignity in drought-affected and displaced communities.ltbrgtlt/pgt
